Synopsis:
In this dialogue, you have killed Nere without doing the duergar mutineers quest. As a result, they want you to pay for the trouble you've caused. You can give them money, persuade them to let you live, or attack.

Cluster Contexts:
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelsExtort.json: You killed Nere off‑screen and never completed the duergar mutineers quest, so a duergar warband led by Kirgrath has intercepted you to demand “restitution” for the trouble you caused. Kirgrath postures violently but is wary of your fighting ability—his men have been stripping the area for loot and intend to haul off prisoners (gnomes/slaves) unless paid or resisted. The clan is jittery about Moonrise forces or other duergar arriving, so they’re in a rush to leave. Companions (Karlach in the samples) may press you to free the captives; your choices are to pay them, try to talk Kirgrath down, or fight the duergar.
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelGreedyExtort.json: You’ve already killed Nere but never completed the duergar mutineers quest, so the duergar treat his death as your crime and demand compensation for the trouble you caused. Elder Brithvar and his clan are on site, tense and ready to leave Moonrise Towers with prisoners and loot — they explicitly claim any gnome slaves as “clan property.” Companions (Karlach appears in the scene; others like Gale might speak up) can argue for the captives or push toward violence. Off‑screen, Nere’s corpse and the captured gnomes/servants (possibly including the elevator gnome Skickpit or other enslaved folk) are present as leverage, and reinforcements or further duergar reprisals could arrive if you refuse to pay or try to bargain. Your immediate choices are to pay them, persuade/intimidate them into letting you live and freeing the captives, or fight.
- UND_DuergarRebelGreedy_AD_CaveInDestroyed.json: Elder Brithvar comments when cave-in is destroyed. Remarks on how it's time he killed Nere if player took mutiny quest.
- UND_TheDrowNere_Mutiny.json: Dialogue after you destroy the cave-in and set Nere free. Thrinn has been put in charge of getting Nere out, but it's the player who accomplishes it. Nere almost just died from inhaling poisonous gas, so he's very angry. In this dialogue, you determine the fate of the gnomes as well as Nere and the mutinous duergar.
- UND_DuergarCamp_LoyalFollowUp.json: You’re at the aftermath of a violent clash in the Emerald Grove: the player had sided with Nere, but both Nere and Thrinn were killed in the fighting, leaving surviving forces scattered and morale low (Novice Grumm’s line reflects that grim discovery). A duergar now steps forward to speak, revealing his intentions for the captive gnomes and putting the party in the position of deciding the gnomes’ fate. Off‑screen the grove is tense — druids led by Kagha are beginning a ritual to cut the place off and tiefling refugees and other figures (trainers like Asharak, leaders like Zevlor) may be nearby or recently involved. You may also have prior contact with the duergar’s small servant gnome (Skickpit) or other NPCs, which can affect available options or how those gnomes are treated. This exchange determines what happens to the gnomes now that the original allies are dead and the grove’s defenders are weakened.
